newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan ruling party plans T$10 bln bank - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan ruling party plans T$10 bln bank - paper.

text.p: The business arm of Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party plans to set up a commercial bank that will be capitalised at T$10 billion, the China Times said on Tuesday.
The party would apply to the finance ministry in October for approval and expected to hold a 30-50 percent stake of the planned bank, the Taipei newspaper said.
A spokesman for Nationalist Party's Business Management Committee declined to comment on the report.
In the early 1990s, Taiwan scrapped a decades-old ban on establishment of commercial banks. Sixteen new banks have started operations since then.
Minimum capitalisation for such a bank is T$10 billion.
The Nationalist Party founded one of the 16, Bank SinoPac, with other investors and initially held 15 percent, though it has trimmed its stake to about five percent, the paper said.
The ruling party also controls around 10 percent of venture capital and investment giant China Development, which plans to convert into an industrial bank.
The Nationalist Party, one of the world's richest with T$85 billion (US$3 billion) in assets, is among Taiwan's leading investors through its seven holding companies.
